lockFileMaintenance.description: package.json carries ranges; package-lock.json is what npm ci installs. Refreshing the lock on a schedule is how transitive dependencies get patched at all — nothing else updates them.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Angular ships framework, CLI, build and CDK as one release train. Bumping them separately produces a tree npm cannot resolve, and @angular/build must move with @angular/cli.
The Angular compiler pins the TypeScript versions it supports, so TypeScript cannot lead an Angular upgrade — it follows one.

The PDF and 3D renderers are loaded from the bundle rather than a CDN (§5.12 A08), so a bump changes shipped bytes in the viewer — the most-used surface in the product. Verify rendering by hand before merging.
Majors are reviewed deliberately. §0.2 still requires acting on them — the dashboard is where they queue, not where they are forgotten.
Let a new patch settle before adopting it; a version yanked within a day should never reach a PR.
